clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death and your move to secondary school, 1991–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather's stroke in June 1991, within three years: you hurt your wrist and stopped playing in the first term at the conservatory, you and Rafe had a blow-up and he moved out, you were getting high and absorbed in fixing radios, you felt lost and low with no footing once he died and your mother was about to remarry, you drifted through a bleak spell at community college, and an exchange in Portugal in early 1994 snapped you out of it. Your father's move toward you and your stepfather's distance from you sit in these months, and your anxiety about his notice rose when you made the chess squad in 1987; the earlier shifts open nothing by themselves.

clusters.name: Your separation from Joelle, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: Around your relationship with Joelle in early 1998, within the year: your insomnia began getting in the way before concerts though you were playing the best you ever had and winning competitions, the relationship ended in July 1999, and you started with a therapist that August. clusters.name: Your separation from Marisol and the slump after, 2001–2008
clusters.reason: Around your burnout from performing and your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, across more than six years: you ran out of steam for performing and grew less content by the month, you had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra and began casting about for what came next, you were on poor terms with family and friends, you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, you met Marisol at a winter party in early 2003 and moved to Fenwick with her by June, you split with her within the year and sank into a deep depression, you returned to Thornbury and could not face your family though you relied gingerly on friends, and you stopped speaking to your mother when you moved to nursing school in August 2008. Your grandmother spent her final months in your parents' home in 2003, and your aunt Imogen had a stroke in 2009. Your functioning fell and your anxiety rose through these years as the family settled into a new balance; the period ends where you turned to your therapist and began to climb out.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death and your cutoff from your mother, 2008–2009
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within a year: you were too drained for conversation at Alder Creek with Silas, your mother pressed to visit you and you kept the door shut on her, you stopped speaking to her when you moved to nursing school that August, and your aunt Imogen had a stroke in 2009. Your distance from your mother and the cutoff that followed sit in these months around your grandmother's loss and your move away.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren and the swamped stretch at her family's lake house, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within more than two years: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along, and in October 2019 around her mother's retirement party at the lake, Wren was swamped with one thing after another, you were too strict laying out a plan to settle her, her family talks all day with nothing happening to one that the others don't hear, you were awake from the small hours at the lake weekend with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose feeling you don't belong, and Wren was anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions. Your anxiety rose around the family gathering and your functioning stayed down; the period ends where things settled once the weekend had a plan.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
